id_and_class.theory_title: Shanahan’s Embodied Insights from Disembodied Minds
id_and_class.summary: Murray Shanahan asks whether consciousness can coherently be attributed to disembodied minds such as LLM-based dialogue agents, which lack bodies and sensory contact with the world. Working from an embodied, enactive view of biological consciousness, he finds that such attributions require a fragmented sense of time and a fractured self, stretching the language of consciousness to breaking point.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness Bound to Body, World and Society

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Biological consciousness arises from the brain–body–world nexus: being in a world and interacting with it, not internal computation alone.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mind, consciousness, intentionality and selfhood are tightly bound to embodiment and environment; cognition is inseparable from the body.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Weak emergence (minds emerge through embodied interaction with the world)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Human subjectivity and selfhood depend on an embodied, social life. For a disembodied dialogue agent, Shanahan argues, any selfhood would be radically fractured and its sense of time profoundly fragmented.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Embodied organisms in physical and social environments; artificial dialogue agents as candidate ‘conscious exotica’ in the space of possible minds.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through philosophical analysis of which conceptions of mind are coherent and intelligible, tested against the unusual properties of contemporary LLM-based agents.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Body, brain and world in continuous interaction, embedded in social life.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal, Selfhood, Subjective time, Artificial and alien minds
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Using disembodied AI as a limit case to reveal how far concepts of consciousness, time and self depend on embodiment and sociality.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Spread across the brain–body–world nexus rather than located in internal computation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Shanahan rejects the assumption that computation alone is both necessary and sufficient for consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Our intuitions about minds are shaped by our evolutionary, embodied and social history, which may lead us to project false coherence onto structures such as disembodied AIs.
core_claims_and_evidence: Much of what we mean by mind, including consciousness, intentionality and selfhood, is bound to embodiment and environment.
A disembodied mind, such as a digital upload, may lack the structure needed to be conscious in any human-comprehensible sense.
Attributing consciousness to LLM agents requires reconciling it with a fragmented sense of time and a fractured selfhood.
Pushing these concepts to their limit yields something like emptiness in the Buddhist sense and weakens dualistic intuitions about subjectivity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and conceptual analysis informed by cognitive robotics and AI

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Shanahan sets out to map the space of possible minds rather than to give a theory of consciousness, so it gives no mechanism for how embodiment produces experience.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Whether a conscious mind can exist without body, world or social embedding remains open; Shanahan treats truly disembodied minds as terra incognita, perhaps inconceivable.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent with embodied and enactive physicalism. His use of Buddhist emptiness to dissolve dualistic intuitions about selfhood fits that stance.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Consciousness in disembodied LLM agents would be either unintelligible or radically alien; Shanahan explores whether any coherent conception fits them without settling the question.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since consciousness here depends on a living body interacting with its world, a mind separated from its body would lack what it needs to be conscious.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Shanahan warns that a mind upload seeking virtual immortality may lack the embodied structure required for human-like consciousness.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Shanahan’s Embodied Insights from Disembodied Minds, Murray Shanahan
